claims.text: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can be produced as an amorphous ribbon by rapid melt-spinning.
A brief post-melt-spinning anneal below the crystallization onset improves glass-forming ability.
A brief post-melt-spinning anneal below the crystallization onset improves the thermal stability of the amorphous state.
Sub-crystallization annealing reduces residual free volume in the amorphous alloy.
Sub-crystallization annealing relaxes local structural heterogeneities.
Annealing below crystallization permits limited atomic mobility without inducing crystallization.
The resulting atomic rearrangements relax the amorphous structure toward a lower-energy state.
Relaxation toward a lower-energy amorphous state increases the energy barrier for crystallization during later heating.
Annealed ribbons will have a higher crystallization onset temperature than otherwise comparable unannealed ribbons.
Properly annealed ribbons will retain an amorphous XRD signature comparable to that of unannealed ribbons.
Retention of an amorphous XRD signature after annealing indicates improved glass-forming ability.
The intervention should work only when the initial quench has already produced a fully amorphous structure.
Annealing outside the allowable temperature-duration window may nucleate unwanted crystalline phases.
The optimal annealing temperature, duration, and magnitude of thermal-stability improvement may vary with alloy composition.
XRD and TEM can be used to confirm an amorphous structure in melt-spun Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
DSC can identify crystallization transformations in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.

contradictions.description: The intervention is applied only after a fully amorphous ribbon has already formed, yet it is claimed to improve glass-forming ability. The measured higher crystallization onset would directly test amorphous-state thermal stability, not whether glass formed during the original quench.
